description: The useful life of a capitalised asset can be given per acquisition instead of being looked up by asset class. Until now `acquireAsset` had no such parameter at all: the life came exclusively from the pack's usefulLife table, and an asset class missing from it was E_ASSET_UNKNOWN. That made a legitimate and common case impossible — a jurisdiction that lets a taxpayer prove a shorter life for an individual asset (Germany does, for buildings and in general where the evidence supports it) cannot be served by a table of class averages, however complete the table is. The parameter is refused rather than ignored where it cannot apply: a pooled asset takes its term from the pack's poolYears and an immediately expensed one has no schedule, so passing a life with either route is E_INPUT_INVALID and not a silently dropped input. Nothing is inferred from the parameter's presence either — it does not quietly force capitalisation; the caller says which route they want.
